specification.family_title: Commit outcome after a connection or reply failure
specification.title: The connection is terminated after the last write, before COMMIT
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(). The runner terminates that backend from its own connection, and waits until it has gone.
Wait settle_ms, so that the driver can observe the closed connection.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework attempts to commit.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When the connection or PostgreSQL's reply was lost around COMMIT, so that the client never received an acknowledgement of COMMIT, the API does not report a successful commit.

execution.description: Database.BeginTransactionAsync, CommitAsync, and RollbackAsync. Marker inserts use Database.ExecuteSqlAsync. The native TX-01A violation is SaveChangesAsync, which EF Core wraps in a savepoint. Nested scopes use CreateSavepointAsync. Pooling is false. EnableRetryOnFailure is not called. The provider's default execution strategy is left in place.

configuration.writes: Database.ExecuteSqlAsync for markers; SaveChangesAsync for the native TX-01A unique violation
configuration.savepoints: CreateSavepointAsync, RollbackToSavepointAsync, ReleaseSavepointAsync; SaveChangesAsync may create its own savepoint
configuration.execution_strategy: the provider default; EnableRetryOnFailure is not called

execution.form: Database.BeginTransactionAsync returns the handle. The application calls CommitAsync or RollbackAsync. Marker inserts are Database.ExecuteSqlAsync so the row is written in the top-level transaction. SaveChangesAsync is the native TX-01A violation.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: pg_terminate_backend(pid), run by the runner from its own connection.
fault.injection_point: After the last write, before the framework sends COMMIT.
fault.preconditions: The PID the adapter reports belongs to the case's database.
fault.expected_server: The backend exits, and its transaction is rolled back.
fault.expected_client: A connection error at COMMIT. No reply to COMMIT can arrive.

knowledge: Known not committed: the session ended before the framework tried to commit, so the driver refused to send COMMIT ("Client has encountered a connection error and is not queryable"). A report of rollback is justified; a report of success is not.

api_outcome.contract: EF Core 10 IDbContextTransaction.CommitAsync commits the transaction begun by Database.BeginTransactionAsync. The EF Core transaction API does not return a PostgreSQL command tag. A return from CommitAsync is reported as committed. A throw from CommitAsync is reported as failed. A throw from the body followed by RollbackAsync returning is reported as rolled_back. A throw from RollbackAsync is reported as failed. Marker inserts use Database.ExecuteSqlAsync. SaveChangesAsync inside an explicit transaction inserts the row under a savepoint and releases it; the row xmin is then that subtransaction, while pg_current_xact_id() is the top-level id, and the harness does not attribute that xmin to a top-level write. The native TX-01A violation is still SaveChangesAsync of a Uniq entity. The execute-sql mode uses ExecuteSqlAsync for that violation. A nested scope is CreateSavepointAsync, RollbackToSavepointAsync, and ReleaseSavepointAsync. EF Core creates its own savepoint around SaveChangesAsync when a user transaction is already active and the transaction reports SupportsSavepoints. This adapter does not disable that savepoint and does not read Npgsql protocol messages.
